thread:
Samir (support): FYI customer INC-12345 having mTLS handshake failures to Redwood Private control plane since cert rotation. They see: "tls: bad certificate" and "handshake failure" in their logs. They report it started ~0400 UTC.

Marta (customer-ops): Confirmed. We pushed a new client cert yesterday and then started seeing errors across all hosts behind our corp egress. Errors from client side: "SSL_connect: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure".

Elaine (oncall): :rotating_light: tagging eng-security. Samir, can you grab the customer s_client output and any server-side control-plane logs? Also ask if they have a TLS inspection proxy / corporate firewall doing TLS terminate/inspect.

Samir (support): Attached abbreviated s_client run they sent (redacted hostnames/IPs):

```
openssl s_client -connect cp.prod.redwood.private:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -servername cp.prod.redwood.private -showcerts -tlsextdebug
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=1 C = US, O = ExampleCA, CN = Example Intermediate
verify error:num=20:unable to verify the first certificate
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=client.example
   i:/CN=Example Intermediate
 1 s:/CN=Example Intermediate
   i:/CN=Example Root
---
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.2
    Cipher    : ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
    Verify return code: 20 (unable to verify the first certificate)
```

They also included control-plane error from their side-proxy: "tls: client certificate required but not provided" for some connections, and for others "client sent no certificate".

Jun (eng-security): Interesting mix. Two immediate suspects: (1) client is not sending full chain / intermediate, so server can't validate -> "unable to verify first certificate"; (2) TLS-terminating proxy (corp MITM) is performing TLS interception and either stripping client certs or breaking mTLS entirely. Also check that our control-plane is in TCP passthrough mode on their private deployment (NLB/ALB misconfig can terminate TLS).

Marta (customer-ops): We do have a ZScaler-like TLS inspection appliance in front of outbound egress. Default behavior there can break client auth. How can we prove that's the issue?

Elaine (oncall): Quick repro steps to ask customer to run (on a failing host):
1) curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key https://cp.prod.redwood.private/health --resolve cp.prod.redwood.private:443:<CP_IP> 
2) openssl s_client -connect <CP_IP>:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -servername cp.prod.redwood.private -state -tlsextdebug -debug > sclient.log 2>&1
3) tcpdump -i <egress_if> host <CP_IP> and send pcap. Look for TLS ClientHello/Certificate messages.

Jun (eng-security): Also ask them to run a zero-terminating test: from a host with no proxy/inspection (e.g., laptop on mobile tether) run the same openssl s_client and compare. If it succeeds off corporate network and fails on-corp, it's almost certainly TLS interception/proxy.

Samir (support): Customer returned additional snippet showing server side (our control plane) log correlation id: rc=cp-7f4a2, remote_addr=<customer-egress-ip>: TLS error: "tls: client did not provide certificate".

Jun (eng-security): That message means our listener got a plain TLS connection with no client cert. If the client definitely has a cert, the likely causes:
- TLS inspection/termination on the egress appliance (strips client cert)
- A load-balancer in front of cp is terminating TLS (ALB in HTTPS mode) and not forwarding client certs to control plane (we need TCP passthrough/NLB or listener configured for mutual TLS)
- Client is misconfigured and not sending client cert chain (missing intermediate).

Elaine (oncall): Action items: Samir to confirm if customer's egress IP is using a TLS interceptor (ask for vendor/config). Jun to check control-plane listener config for this Private deployment (is there an NLB vs ALB difference?). I'll set priority P1 until we confirm.

Samir (support): Customer confirms egress appliance = "CorpProxy v3.2" doing outbound TLS inspection. They can whitelist destination but say the appliance negotiates TLS with external server and re-signs, which likely removes client certs. They asked if we can support a mode to accept proxied connections.

Jun (eng-security): We cannot accept proxied TLS that strips client certs because mTLS relies on end-to-end client certificate presentation. Two options for customer:
- Configure their proxy as TLS passthrough for the control-plane host(s) so the original client certificate reaches Redwood (preferred).
- Termination + re-issue: the proxy must forward the original client cert (rare) via X-Client-Cert header over a mutually trusted channel — but that requires a custom, insecure integration and is not supported by default.

Marta (customer-ops): They asked for exact firewall allowlist and SNI to whitelist. What do we give them?

Elaine (oncall): Provide them with: destination IP range: <CP_IP>/32 (we gave exact IPs in DM), port 443, required SNI: cp.prod.redwood.private, allow TLS passthrough (no TLS intercept), and ensure they allow the full certificate chain from clients (don't strip intermediates). Also ask them to confirm time sync (expired client cert can give similar errors).

Samir (support): Customer performed test from mobile tether — s_client succeeded and control-plane accepted client cert. From corp egress same host fails. They will raise a ticket with their proxy team to disable interception for cp.prod.redwood.private.

Elaine (oncall): Great repro. Please collect the following and attach to INC-12345: failing s_client output, successful s_client (mobile), control-plane correlation logs, tcpdump pcap if possible, and the proxy vendor/config lines showing interception. We'll keep P1 until proxy whitelist confirmed. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident INC-12345 set to priority P1 by Elaine (oncall).

Jun (eng-security): Follow-up notes for postmortem: we should document guidance for Private customers with strict egress policies: explicit support doc for mTLS and TLS-passthrough, FAQ on corporate TLS-inspection appliances, and checklist for support engineers (openssl commands, logs to collect). I'll draft a doc after this is closed.

Samir (support): Copying summary back to customer: we believe cause = corporate TLS inspection stripping client certificates. Next step is to request passthrough whitelist. Will update ticket when done.

Marta (customer-ops): Will update when proxy team confirms. Thanks all. :eyes:
